model_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: The MacBook Air with Apple M4 has 16 GB unified memory and relies on CPU/Metal acceleration. Among the candidate architectures, yolov8 offers a favorable balance of detection quality and runtime efficiency on such hardware, with established workflows for CoreML/Metal deployment. It generally provides better accuracy than lightweight single-stage nets like SSD300 while remaining more CPU-friendly than heavier two-stage models (FasterRCNN/RetinaNet) and large RTDETR variants. Given the target mAP@0.5:0.95 around 0.30 and the need to run entirely locally, yolov8 is the most practical baseline that can reach the target with proper preprocessing and potential model size tuning (e.g., resolution, input scale) without requiring GPU acceleration. The other candidates are considered for fallback if yolov8 underperforms in practice or if deployment tooling limitations arise on macOS.

dataset_selection_decision_evidence.rationale: Strategy summary: Use a single strong, domain-aligned primary pool (BDD100K Detection Train) for all classes to maximize domain fidelity to traffic scenes and reduce leakage risk. Do not select derived day/night BDD variants due to mutual-exclusivity constraints with the primary pool. Allocate 2500 images from BDD100K for five classes (car, bus, truck, bicycle, pedestrian). For motorcycle, BDD100K provides 2327 images, which is below the target of 2500, so add a single generalization source (LVIS) to meet the minimum mixed-source requirements and improve diversity. LVIS contributes 500 images to motorcycle, yielding 2327 + 500 = 2827 total motorcycle samples, which stays within the 3000 per-class cap and satisfies the policy’s domain-mix requirements (primary-domain share ~0.82, above the 0.8 preferred minimum). This plan uses at most one generalization source per class (maximum_generalization_sources = 1) and adheres to the mutually_exclusive_source_pairs constraints by excluding derived/bdd-cycleGAN day2night variants. Dataset counts chosen are all <= the available_count for each source/class combination (e.g., 2500 <= 68943 for car, 2500 <= 2327 for motorcycle from primary plus 500 from LVIS). Total approximate download footprint (counting per-class allocations and avoiding double-counting across classes) is about 15,327 images (BDD100K: 14,827 images across all classes; LVIS: 500 images as motorcycle generalization). The approach aims for a practical target similar to 2,500 per class while satisfying diversity and domain-alignment constraints. No explicit download-budget constraint was provided; if budget is tight, we can reduce the motorcycle mix to exactly 2327 from BDD100K and drop LVIS, staying at 2327 for that class within the 2000–3000 range.

hyperparameter_decision_evidence.rationale: Initial executable config for CPU/Metal deployment on Apple Silicon (M4). Yolov8_n provides a favorable accuracy/compute balance for traffic scenes in this constrained hardware context. Data splits are aligned with the predefined per-class pools (BDD100K primary, LVIS supplemental for motorcycle) to reach ~2500 images per class while preserving domain fidelity and reducing leakage. The schedule and hyperparameters are chosen to be safe and conservative for CPU inference, ensuring a meaningful training phase within realistic compute limits. All fields are kept within standard detection training practices and respect the provided performance target (mAP@0.5:0.95 ~ 0.3).
